clue.text: It will spoil a short drink to leave it on one side

definitions.text: to leave it on one side

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil or damage it
gin is a short, a spirit served in a small measure rather than a long drink

explanation.surface: A warning that some ingredient will ruin a quick nip unless it is kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'short' in British pubs is a spirit such as gin, as opposed to a long drink like beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is the blank border of a page, space deliberately kept clear at the side.

clue.text: Think to prepare a paper during tea in S. America

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time of the other, so goes inside it

parts.note: mate is the herbal tea drunk in South America
to edit is to prepare a newspaper or text for publication

explanation.surface: Musing over writing an article while drinking tea in Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect or ponder deeply.

clue.text: Yet again "Go hang!" in the House

definitions.text: Yet again "Go hang!" in the House

parts.words: Yet again "Go hang!" in the House
parts.note: sounds like an exasperated curse, but means hang wallpaper once more inside the home

explanation.definitionFit: To repaper a room is to hang fresh wallpaper on its walls again.

clue.text: A meet thing to' do at a party

definitions.text: A meet thing to' do at a party

parts.words: A meet thing to' do at a party
parts.note: meet means proper, but the fitting thing is making guests meet each other

explanation.definitionFit: To introduce people is to make them known to one another by name.

clue.text: Seaman 'sent east twice — and he's gone

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
E is the compass abbreviation for east
twice says the east abbreviation is given a second time

explanation.surface: A sailor posted eastward on two occasions has now departed.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is away or missing from where they should be.

clue.text: Request one unflashy automobile to go to Asia for a song

parts.note: to beg is to request
dull means unflashy, plain
a car is an automobile
E, for East, stands for Asia

explanation.surface: Asking for a plain car to drive to Asia in exchange for very little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begone, Dull Care' is an old English song; 'for a song' looks like cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone, Dull Care is a traditional English ballad, a piece of music to be sung.

clue.text: How Myra, say, might ditch a lover?

definitions.text: How Myra, say, might ditch a lover?

parts.words: How Myra, say, might ditch a lover?
parts.note: Myra said aloud is mirer, one who mires, and such a person would dump a lover by sinking him in a swamp

explanation.definitionFit: To embog is to sink or trap in a bog, much as one might mire someone.

clue.text: Shy Sally seen in the,…fashion in town

parts.note: a shy and a sally are both jibes or gibes, so together a taunt
on can mean fashionable, in vogue

explanation.surface: A timid girl named Sally spotted in trendy clothes around town.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUNTON is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is an English county town in Somerset.

clue.text: Admission — one's dished!

definitions.meaning: the right to enter a place
a dish that is served up at a meal

explanation.definitionFit: Entree means right of entry, and also a course served at dinner.

clue.text: Make top-grade 'sapper an officer-member '. of the corps

parts.note: make an officer, i.e. commission, by granting the rank
A1 means top-grade, with the figure 1 read as letter I
RE, Royal Engineers, are the sappers of the British Army

explanation.surface: Promote a first-rate army engineer to officer rank within his corps.
explanation.walkthrough: The Corps of Commissionaires is a British body of uniformed doormen, originally ex-servicemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissionaire is a uniformed doorkeeper, traditionally a member of the Corps of Commissionaires.

clue.text: Siamese vowel-sounds?

parts.note: joined-together vowel sounds, like Siamese twins: two vowels fused into one glide in a single syllable

explanation.definitionFit: A diphthong is a gliding speech unit in which two vowel qualities are joined within one syllable.

clue.text: Report that a beast, is heard

indicators.note: is heard says the word for a beast is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a brute is a savage animal or beast

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that an animal can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To bruit is to spread news about, so as a noun it is a rumour or piece of news.

clue.text: " The Cock " bar?

parts.note: read as a pub sign, but a cock is also a tap, so a bar named after one is a room where drink is drawn

explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is the public bar of an inn, where beer is served from the cask.

clue.text: Near thing to wear round the neck for sleep

parts.note: nigh is an old word meaning near

parts.words: thing to wear round the neck
parts.note: a tie is the strip of cloth worn knotted round the neck

explanation.surface: Advice about putting on neckwear before going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown, in its familiar short form, is the garment worn in bed for sleeping.

clue.text: Port to celebrate Finnish- Ottoman union?

parts.note: the Ottoman Empire was the Turkish empire, so an Ottoman is a Turk

explanation.surface: A harbour town where Finland and the Ottomans might mark a joint alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finnish' tells you the port is in Finland, though it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Turku is a seaport city on the south-west coast of Finland.

clue.text: Audibly heaved sad breaths protractedly, giving. such glances

indicators.note: audibly says the phrase for long sighs is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: heaving sad breaths for a long time is to have sighed long

explanation.surface: Someone sighing heavily while casting sly looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidelong glances are looks directed sideways, out of the corner of the eye.

clue.text: Publicity film ?

explanation.definitionFit: Being in the limelight is being in public view; Limelight is also a Charlie Chaplin picture.

clue.text: Don't be thoughtless, study carefully, red, is coming up

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up says these words read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to think: study hard, the red is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns RED IS into SIDER, after CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Consider is an instruction to think carefully, the opposite of being heedless.

clue.text: Indictment of the faithful Willie

parts.note: true means faithful or loyal
Willie and Bill are both pet forms of William

explanation.surface: A charge brought against a loyal man named William.
explanation.walkthrough: A true bill was the endorsement a grand jury gave a charge it found well founded.
explanation.definitionFit: A true bill is a bill of indictment that a grand jury has endorsed as sound.

clue.text: Dick is one of the pack in Brazil

indicators.note: in says the card goes inside the Brazilian city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is Brazil's famous city
a card is one of a pack of playing cards

explanation.surface: A man named Dick is one of a gang operating in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricardo is the Spanish and Portuguese form of Richard, of which Dick is a pet name.

clue.text: It means progress for Parisians Down Under

definitions.text: It means progress for Parisians Down Under

parts.words: It means progress for Parisians Down Under
parts.note: seems to be about Australia, but means a way of getting about beneath the streets of Paris

explanation.definitionFit: The Paris underground railway is the city's network of trains running below ground.

clue.text: Opera hero didn't date Ann though — hear that?

indicators.note: hear that says the phrase for a meeting with Ann is spoken, giving a sound-alike name

parts.note: to date Ann is to tryst Ann

explanation.surface: A tenor role who never went out with a girl called Ann.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's Tristan meets Isolde, not Ann, hence 'didn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan is the title role of Wagner's opera Tristan und Isolde.

clue.text: Etonian cricketer hardly describes Robert Burns

definitions.meaning: at Eton a boy who plays cricket rather than rowing
the Scottish poet Burns was a hard drinker, so not a teetotal Bob

explanation.definitionFit: At Eton College a dry bob plays land sports, a wet bob rows; Burns, a Robert, was no abstainer.

clue.text: Disturbance — that would, be teacher's. aim after this month

indicators.note: after says the part left over is what follows this month's abbreviation

parts.note: a teacher aims to give instruction
inst., instant, is the old commercial-letter abbreviation for this month

explanation.surface: Trouble that a teacher would aim to sort out once the month is over.
explanation.walkthrough: In old business letters 'inst.' (instant) meant this month; remove INST from the front of INSTRUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy quarrel or uproar.

clue.text: Why nitre can't' change when' it does

definitions.text: Why nitre can't' change when' it does

indicators.note: change says the letters of the chemical name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle: why can't saltpetre alter, when in fact it does?
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranged, NITRE becomes the word saying it is unreactive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert is chemically unreactive, unable to change.

clue.text: The commandant has false reports: on-dogs'

parts.note: Col, colonel, is the rank of a commanding officer
lies are false statements

explanation.surface: A commanding officer spreads untruths about canines.
explanation.definitionFit: Collies are sheepdogs, a breed of herding dog.

clue.text: Boat 'for bumping' races?

parts.note: bumping races are rowing contests where crews chase to bump the boat ahead; to bump or push clumsily is also the verb sense

explanation.walkthrough: In Oxford and Cambridge bumping races, eights try to touch the boat in front; to barge is also to shove.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed boat, and to barge is to bump into people roughly.

clue.text: Arid, Reg? It could be watered:

indicators.note: could be says the letters of these words might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Asking a man named Reg whether dry land might be given water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ARID, REG and IT together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Irrigated land has had water supplied to it by channels or pipes.

clue.text: Wellingtonia?

parts.note: Wellingtonia is a giant sequoia, but read as something for Wellington boots it is a shoe-shaped wooden form

explanation.walkthrough: Wellingtonia is a giant redwood; Wellingtons are rubber boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot tree is a shaped form put inside a boot to keep it in shape.

clue.text: He makes amends-soon after midday: right?.

parts.note: at one o'clock is soon after midday

explanation.surface: A man apologising just after noon, asking if he has it correct.
explanation.definitionFit: One who atones makes reparation for a wrong.
